sections.h2: Where to find the Bedford County Register of Deeds
sections.html:
Visit Suite 303 at 100 West Side Square in Shelbyville, TN 37160, or reach the office by phone at (931) 684-5719 or fax at (931) 685-2086. Both numbers appear on the county's contact page.

This is where the public record of who owns what is kept, along with liens and contracts. Money comes in through recording and filing fees and through a commission on the conveyance and mortgage taxes the office collects for the state, which it remits monthly. Details are on the register of deeds page.

Sellers can use two tools there. A fee calculator lets you estimate costs before recording. A free fraud alert notifies you when a transfer is filed under your name, and it accepts several spellings or forms of a name, including nicknames and suffixes. Anyone who owns a seldom-visited property, an inherited one for example, gains peace of mind from signing up.

Southern Middle Tennessee is home to Bedford County, which sits inside the Nashville-Davidson-Murfreesboro combined statistical area. Shelbyville serves as seat and sole city, while Bell Buckle, Normandy and Wartrace are towns. Estimated population for 2025 is 55,273, a gain of 10.0 percent from April 2020. Owners occupy 71.9 percent of the 21,876 housing units, and the median owner-occupied home is worth $281,200 for 2020 to 2024.

Tennessee's realty transfer tax is $0.37 per $100. The buyer pays at recording, and the amount is measured differently for each kind of deed.

Deed typeTax base
Warranty deed or other freehold transferWhichever is greater, the consideration or the property's value at transfer
Quitclaim deedThe consideration given, unless the deed's wording shows the grantor meant to convey the property itself
Warranty deed with a retained life estateFair market value less the value of the life estate
Modified or amended deedMust cite the earlier deed's book and page, proving the original tax was paid

Wording such as "to have and to hold" or "in fee simple" may move a quitclaim deed to the fair market value basis. If a seller keeps a life estate, the preparer values that estate and subtracts it, which shrinks the base. Your closing attorney handles that calculation. A normal sale is taxed on what was actually paid or what the property is worth.

Someone on the buying side, whether the buyer, an agent or a trustee, takes an oath at the register's counter. They state the actual consideration or the property's value, whichever is larger, and the statement goes on the face of the deed. If a transfer is exempt, the oath is skipped. Knowingly stating a false figure can lead to a perjury charge.

For fair market value the state looks to the tax base on file at the assessor's office, and it will also take a recent appraisal that office has accepted. Reporting less than that opens the door to an audit plus penalties and interest. Reviewers pick counties at random, pull recorded deeds, compare the sworn number with the assessor value on the Comptroller's website, and may send the person named on the deed an inquiry letter.

No one pays twice for one transaction. If several deeds cover a single transfer of one parcel, the tax is paid once, and nothing is owed until title really passes by deed.

Among the transfers that owe nothing:

  • An executor's deed that carries out a will
  • A deed or decree settling a divorce
  • A life estate released to the remainder beneficiaries
  • Placement in, or return from, a revocable living trust by the same transferor or spouse

sections.h2: If the buyer takes out a loan
sections.html:
A deed of trust triggers a mortgage tax, separate from the transfer tax, of $0.115 per $100 of debt with $2,000 excluded. The borrower pays, and the register holds the instrument until payment is made. Each recorded instrument showing a debt must include this sentence: "Maximum principal indebtedness for Tennessee recording tax purposes is $___."

Loan assumptions are treated their own way. Suppose a buyer takes over your loan. If you stay liable on the old debt, no new tax applies. If the buyer signs a fresh agreement with the lender and your obligation is cancelled, the new mortgage is taxed. Anyone who fails to pay the tax owes $250 or twice the unpaid amount, whichever is more.

Mechanics, contractor, subcontractor and laborer liens and judgment liens are not subject to the mortgage tax. They can still hang over the title, so have the title company search for them well ahead of closing.

Valuation is handled on the third floor of the courthouse annex at 100 West Side Square, Suite 301, by the Property Assessor, (931) 684-6390. The assessor values real estate and business personal property, maintains tax maps and builds the tax rolls that go to the trustee and the towns. A value you dispute goes first to the local board of equalization and, if unresolved, to the State Board of Equalization.

Bills are paid at the Trustee's office, first floor of the annex, 100 Public Square West, Suite 102, phone (931) 684-4303. Weekday hours are 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. In January and February Saturday hours from 8 a.m. to noon are added for payments. Online payment is available through a link on the county page. The trustee also administers the Tax Relief Program, which dates to 1976 and helps homeowners who are 65 or older, homeowners who are disabled and those with a permanent service-related disability.

The state calendar governs Bedford County. Assessment is as of January 1. The current year's bill is payable from the first Monday in October. Last year's bill turns delinquent on March 1, which makes the end of February the final day to pay with no interest.

With a sale pending, ask the trustee where the account stands. Any unpaid balance is subtracted from your proceeds at closing. Get the figure early and pass it along to the title company.

sections.h2: Selling a Bedford County house for cash
sections.html:
Some owners pick a cash sale to dodge repairs, showings and the wait for a buyer's financing. We buy Bedford County houses as-is. The deal still finishes at the Register of Deeds, so the recording rules above govern it: a proper deed, the oath of value and the transfer tax. No lender means no mortgage tax.

Round up your deed or its recording details, your latest tax bill and payoff amounts for any loan. If the house came through an estate, add the executor's papers. If the house sits vacant, enroll in the fraud alert so any recorded transfer under your name reaches you quickly.

faqs.q: What is the address of the Bedford County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: It is Suite 303 at 100 West Side Square, Shelbyville, TN 37160, and the phone is (931) 684-5719. An online fee calculator is linked from the county page.

faqs.q: How is the transfer tax figured on a Bedford County home sale?
faqs.a: The buyer pays $0.37 per $100 of the higher of the price or the property's value. Quitclaim deeds are measured on the consideration unless the wording conveys the property itself.

faqs.q: Is any Bedford County transfer exempt from the realty transfer tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Executor's deeds under a will, divorce settlement deeds and transfers into or out of a revocable living trust by the same person or spouse are among those listed. An exempt transfer needs no oath of value.

faqs.q: Can I get an alert if someone records a deed in my name?
faqs.a: Yes. Sign up for the register's free fraud alert and you will be notified of transfers filed under your name. Several name variations can be enrolled.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Bedford County property tax?
faqs.a: Go to the Trustee at 100 Public Square West, Suite 102, or use the online link on the trustee's page. The office is open weekdays 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. and Saturday mornings in January and February. The number is (931) 684-4303.
